explanation: A thumbs-up is widely understood in Germany as a friendly, informal signal of approval or agreement, just as in most Western countries, and it's used comfortably in everyday life and casual business settings. One quirk: Germans also raise the thumb to mean 'one' when counting on their fingers, so it can briefly read as a number rather than approval out of context.
local_tip: Use it freely for casual agreement, but in very formal settings a nod or spoken confirmation comes across as more professional.

also_check.note: The gesture is considered a serious obscene insult, roughly equivalent to showing the middle finger.
Among older generations it can be read as a vulgar insult similar to 'up yours,' though younger Greeks mostly take it as 'OK' today.
Thumbs-up is a universally positive, casual gesture with no real risk of offense.
